messages.text:
"Create a fully playable 2D pixel-art 3v3 ninja MOBA game inspired by Naruto.

GRAPHICS AND STYLE

- 2D top-down camera view.
- Small, colorful pixel-art characters, similar to classic top-down RPG games.
- Detailed pixel-art animations.
- Green grass, trees, rocks and village environments.
- Naruto-inspired visual design.
- Smooth movement and combat animations.
- Characters must be small on the screen, not large anime portraits or 3D models.

GAMEPLAY

- 3 versus 3 real-time battles.
- The player directly controls one hero.
- Virtual joystick on the left side of the screen.
- Attack and ability buttons on the right side.
- Two allied AI teammates.
- Three enemy AI-controlled heroes.
- Health bars and chakra bars.
- Each match should have a clear victory and defeat condition.
- Enemies should actively fight, chase and defend themselves.

CHARACTERS
Include Naruto, Sasuke, Sakura, Kakashi, Itachi and other Naruto characters.

Each character must have:

- Unique pixel-art sprite.
- Unique basic attack.
- Three special abilities.
- Different attack animations.
- Different movement speed and combat statistics.

SPECIAL ABILITIES
Naruto:

- Shadow Clone Jutsu.
- Rasengan.
- Nine-Tails Chakra.

Sasuke:

- Chidori.
- Fire Style.
- Sharingan.

Sakura:

- Super Strength.
- Healing.
- Powerful Ground Punch.

Kakashi:

- Lightning Blade.
- Sharingan.
- Earth Style.

ARENA

- Create a large top-down pixel-art battlefield.
- Add trees, rocks, grass and destructible objects.
- Include obstacles that characters cannot walk through.
- Add a Naruto-inspired village map.

PROGRESSION

- Character selection screen.
- Unlockable heroes.
- Character levels.
- Different skins.
- Experience and rewards after battles.

IMPORTANT
Make this a real playable mobile game, not just a static image or visual demonstration.

Prioritize functional movement, combat, AI opponents and abilities before adding extra features.

Use portrait or landscape mobile layout depending on what works best for the gameplay.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a fully playable, mobile-friendly 2D pixel-art 3v3 ninja MOBA inspired by Naruto, prioritizing movement, combat, AI, and abilities.

## Requirements
- Include character selection, six Naruto-inspired heroes with unique attacks and three abilities, two allied AI, three enemy AI, health/chakra, victory/defeat, destructible obstacles, and progression/unlocks.
- Provide keyboard and mobile touch controls; make reasonable assumptions and do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Created a dependency-free vanilla HTML/CSS/Canvas game from scratch because the repository had no application source or framework.
- Used a landscape arena with a responsive mobile layout and hand-drawn pixel-art sprites and terrain.

## Work State

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a fully playable, mobile-friendly 2D pixel-art 3v3 ninja MOBA inspired by Naruto, prioritizing movement, combat, AI, and abilities.

## Requirements
- Include six heroes with unique attacks and abilities, two allied AI, three enemy AI, health/chakra, match outcomes, destructible obstacles, and progression/unlocks.
- Support keyboard and mobile touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Built a dependency-free vanilla HTML/CSS/Canvas game because the repository had no application source or framework.
- Used a landscape arena, responsive layout, and hand-drawn pixel-art sprites and terrain.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented hero selection, squad HUD, progression and unlocks persisted in localStorage, 3v3 combat and AI, abilities, projectiles, collisions, and win/loss conditions.
- Added WASD/arrow keys, Space/J attack, number keys for abilities, and mobile joystick/action buttons.
- Made destructible props take hits from basic attacks and projectiles; added an inline favicon to avoid the missing favicon request.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`; captured desktop and mobile selection screenshots and reviewed layout.

### Active
- Do a deeper gameplay check, especially prop destruction, ability interactions, and match completion; mobile touch controls remain unverified in a live match.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test a live match through victory/defeat and exercise abilities and destructible props.
2. Confirm touch controls in a mobile-sized live match and check for browser console errors.
3. Report the game and any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface, selection/result overlays, HUD, and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Canvas rendering, heroes, combat, AI, abilities, input, destructible props, and progression.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile presentation.
- `/tmp/opencode/shinobi-battle.jpg`: Earlier gameplay screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/shinobi-desktop.png`: Recent desktop selection screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/shinobi-mobile.png`: Recent mobile selection screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are currently untracked.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- The earlier browser test reported `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)`; an inline favicon was added afterward, but the browser console has not been rechecked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a fully playable, mobile-friendly 2D pixel-art 3v3 ninja MOBA inspired by Naruto, prioritizing movement, combat, AI, and abilities.

## Requirements
- Six heroes with unique attacks and abilities, two allied AI, three enemy AI, health/chakra, match outcomes, destructible obstacles, and progression/unlocks.
- Support keyboard and mobile touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use dependency-free vanilla HTML/CSS/Canvas because the repository had no application source or framework.
- Use a responsive landscape arena with hand-drawn pixel-art sprites and terrain.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented hero selection, squad HUD, progression and unlocks persisted in localStorage, 3v3 combat and AI, abilities, projectiles, collisions, and win/loss conditions.
- Added keyboard and touch controls, destructible props, and an inline favicon.
- Fixed AI target scanning so units pursue opponents across the arena instead of stopping when enemies are beyond 430 units.
- Passed `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and browser gameplay checks for prop damage, abilities, victory/defeat outcomes, XP reward, mobile-layout controls, and movement.
- Browser checks reported no console or page errors; an actual 23-second battle ran without errors, and a 10-second diagnostic confirmed allied and enemy AI movement.

### Active
- Confirm match completion during a natural, uninterrupted match; assess player movement when obstacles are encountered.
- Verify controls using actual mobile touch input, beyond the emulated pointer drag.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run a longer natural match and confirm it reaches victory or defeat.
2. Check mobile controls with touch input in a live match and investigate any movement sticking.
3. Report remaining limitations and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Gameplay logic and AI pursuit fix.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Game interface, selection/result overlays, HUD, and touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: Desktop and mobile presentation.
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: Browser checks for combat, destructible props, match outcomes, and emulated mobile controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/live-match-check.mjs`: Natural-match browser smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/ai-diagnostic.mjs`: AI position diagnostic.

## Important Context
- The game files are uncommitted and currently untracked.
- A local server is running at `http://127.0.0.1:3002`.
- The 23-second natural match remained 3–3 with the player’s health unchanged; the AI diagnostic afterward showed allies and enemies had moved toward each other.

## Objective
- Build a fully playable, mobile-friendly 2D pixel-art 3v3 ninja MOBA inspired by Naruto, prioritizing movement, combat, AI, and abilities.

## Requirements
- Six heroes with unique attacks and abilities; two allied AI and three enemy AI; health, chakra, match outcomes, destructible obstacles, and progression/unlocks.
- Support keyboard and mobile touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use dependency-free vanilla HTML/CSS/Canvas because the repository had no application source or framework.
- Use a responsive landscape arena with hand-drawn pixel-art sprites and terrain.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented hero selection, squad HUD, progression/unlocks in localStorage, 3v3 combat and AI, abilities, projectiles, collisions, win/loss conditions, destructible props, keyboard/touch controls, and responsive presentation.
- Previous gameplay checks passed for prop damage, abilities, victory/defeat outcomes, XP reward, and mobile layout.
- Diagnosed natural-match AI blockage at the central village obstacle and actual mobile joystick pointer cancellation.
- Updated `game.js` AI movement with a top/bottom village detour waypoint; this latest change is not yet verified.

### Active
- Fix mobile joystick cancellation by adding `touch-action: none` to `.stick-zone` in `style.css`, then rerun the real-touch check.
- Verify AI detours allow engagements and a natural match to reach victory or defeat; investigate further if units remain stuck.
- Rerun syntax, diff, and browser gameplay checks after fixes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add `touch-action: none` to `.stick-zone` in `style.css`; rerun `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs` and confirm sustained touch movement and skill activation.
2. Run an instrumented match to verify AI units cross the central village using the new route in `game.js`; fix route issues if necessary.
3. Run a longer natural match and confirm it reaches victory/defeat; then rerun existing checks and report results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: gameplay and the unverified AI waypoint detour.
- `style.css`: mobile joystick styling; touch cancellation fix remains pending.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: live-match touch input check.
- `/tmp/opencode/ai-touch-diagnostic.mjs`: captures touch events and AI positions.
- `/tmp/opencode/long-match-check.mjs`: natural-match smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: automated gameplay assertions.

## Important Context
- Game files are uncommitted and untracked.
- A 2-minute natural match remained live at 3–3; allies and enemies were stuck on opposite sides of the central village, whose solid props block direct paths.
- Real touch input triggered `pointercancel`; the joystick reset to zero, and the player moved only about 1.4 units during an 800 ms drag.
- `game.js` has just been edited to route cross-village AI via a top or bottom lane. No post-edit tests have been run yet.

Continue developing the existing 2D pixel-art Naruto-inspired 3v3 MOBA game. Do not rebuild or replace the existing game. Add a complete Hero Transformation System.

Transformation mechanics


- Every hero with a transformation has a special transformation bar.
- The bar fills by dealing damage, defeating enemies, and participating in fights.
- When the bar is full, the player can activate the transformation using a special button.
- Transformations last for a limited time.
- During transformation, the hero gets a new appearance, stronger abilities, unique animations, and improved stats.
- When the transformation ends, the hero returns to normal.
- Add a cooldown before the next transformation.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Continue the existing 2D pixel-art 3v3 game and add a complete, mobile-friendly hero transformation system without replacing the game.

## Requirements
- Transformations charge through damage, defeats, and fight participation; become activatable when full; have limited duration and cooldown.
- Each specified hero gets distinct transformed visuals, animations, stronger transformed abilities, stats, and start/end visual and sound effects.
- Keep transformations powerful but balanced; heroes without transformations remain playable.
- Transformation bar, button, abilities, and animations must work on mobile.

## Decisions
- Build on the existing dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game and preserve its roster and gameplay.
- Transformation UI uses an arena HUD meter/button; intended keyboard activation is `T`, with mobile activation via the same visible button.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing game baseline: hero selection, 3v3 AI combat, abilities, progression, obstacles, keyboard/touch controls, and responsive presentation.
- Added transformation HUD markup to `index.html` and appended responsive transformation-widget styles to `style.css`.
- Added seven heroes to `game.js` (Jiraiya, Rock Lee, Gaara, Orochimaru, Madara, Obito, Killer Bee) while retaining the existing roster.
- Added transformation configuration for all ten requested heroes.
- Added initial transformation-state fields to each unit.

### Active
- Integrate charge generation, activation, cooldown and duration; transformed stats, sprite/effects, sounds, and transformed skill behavior.
- Wire HUD/button and keyboard/mobile controls; finish roster count/selection presentation.
- Run syntax, gameplay, and mobile checks; changes are uncommitted.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue integrating transformation lifecycle, charge, AI activation, and combat attribution in `game.js`.
2. Implement transformed skill variants, visual effects/animations, and start/end audio.
3. Connect and update transformation HUD states, then test desktop and mobile gameplay.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing game and in-progress hero/transformation data and state changes.
- `index.html`: Transformation meter/button markup.
- `style.css`: Transformation HUD styles and mobile layout.
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: Existing gameplay assertions.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: Existing touch-control check.
- `/tmp/opencode/long-match-check.mjs`: Existing match smoke test.

## Important Context
- The original game had six heroes; the new data retains those and adds seven, yielding thirteen total.
- Existing transformation integration is incomplete and has not been tested; do not treat the HUD/data additions as a finished feature.

## Objective
- Complete the existing 2D pixel-art 3v3 game with a mobile-friendly hero transformation system while preserving its roster and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Transformations charge through damage, defeats, and fight participation; become activatable when full; have limited duration and cooldown.
- Specified heroes need distinct transformed visuals, animations, stronger abilities, improved stats, and start/end visual and sound effects.
- Keep transformations powerful but balanced; heroes without transformations remain playable.
- Transformation bar, button, abilities, and animations must work on mobile.

## Decisions
- Build on the existing dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game.
- Transformation activation uses `T` on keyboard and the visible button on mobile.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added transformation HUD markup and responsive styling; fixed the widget lookup by adding `id="transform-widget"`.
- Expanded the roster to 13 heroes and added transformation configurations for 10 heroes.
- Added transformation state and helper functions for charge, activation, transformed stats/skills, effects, sound, and HUD updates.
- Updated the displayed roster count to `13`.
- Integrated transformation duration/cooldown and nearby-fight charge updates into `update()`, plus AI activation and transformed skill selection.
- Updated movement speed and basic attack range/power to use transformed stats.

### Active
- Integrate damage, takedown, and participation charge attribution into combat.
- Finish transformed skill effects, visuals, animations, and transformation HUD/button/`T` input wiring.
- Run desktop and mobile gameplay checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add charge gain and transformed defense/guard handling in `damageTarget()`; attribute takedowns and damage to attackers.
2. Finish transformed skill effects and transformed hero rendering/animation feedback.
3. Wire the HUD button and `T` key; verify transformation HUD updates throughout battle.
4. Run syntax checks and the available gameplay, touch, and long-match checks.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: Desktop and mobile gameplay assertions.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: Touch-control check.
- `/tmp/opencode/long-match-check.mjs`: Long-match smoke test.

## Important Context
- Changes remain uncommitted; earlier `git status --short` showed project files as untracked.
- `game.js` currently has partial lifecycle and transformed-stat integration; damage attribution, transformed skills/visuals, and input wiring remain unfinished.
- Existing browser checks expect a local game server at `http://127.0.0.1:3002`.

## Objective
- Complete the existing 2D pixel-art 3v3 game with mobile-friendly hero transformations while preserving its roster and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Transformations charge through damage, defeats, and fight participation; become activatable when full; and have limited duration and cooldown.
- Specified heroes need distinct transformed visuals, animations, stronger abilities, improved stats, and start/end visual and sound effects.
- Keep transformations powerful but balanced; heroes without transformations remain playable.
- Transformation bar, button, abilities, and animations must work on mobile.

## Decisions
- Build on the existing dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game.
- Transformation activation uses `T` on keyboard and the visible button on mobile.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added transformation HUD, responsive styling, 13-hero roster, and transformations for 10 heroes.
- Implemented transformation charging/lifecycle, stat and skill changes, effects, sound, visuals, HUD, and keyboard/mobile activation.
- Fixed the missing `transform-meter` ID that caused a browser error.
- `node --check game.js` passed; desktop gameplay, mobile gameplay, and live touch-control checks passed with no browser errors.

### Active
- Validate transformation activation, transformed skills/visuals, charge attribution, balance, and long-match behavior.
- Review the final diff.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `/tmp/opencode/long-match-check.mjs` and transformation-specific checks.
2. Fix any issues found and review the final diff.
3. Summarize the uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Transformation lifecycle, combat, transformed skills, HUD, input, and visuals.
- `index.html`: Transformation HUD markup.
- `style.css`: Transformation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: Desktop and mobile gameplay assertions.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: Live touch-control check.
- `/tmp/opencode/long-match-check.mjs`: Long-match smoke test.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Browser checks use `http://127.0.0.1:3002`.
- The long-match and transformation-specific checks are still pending.

## Objective
- Complete the existing 2D pixel-art 3v3 game with mobile-friendly hero transformations while preserving its roster and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Transformations charge through damage, defeats, and fight participation; become activatable when full; and have limited duration and cooldown.
- Specified heroes need distinct transformed visuals, animations, stronger abilities, improved stats, and start/end visual and sound effects.
- Keep transformations powerful but balanced; heroes without transformations remain playable.
- Transformation bar, button, abilities, and animations must work on mobile.

## Decisions
- Build on the existing dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game.
- Transformation activation uses `T` on keyboard and the visible button on mobile.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added transformation HUD, responsive styling, 13-hero roster, and transformations for 10 heroes.
- Implemented transformation charging/lifecycle, stat and skill changes, effects, sound, visuals, HUD, keyboard/mobile activation.
- Fixed missing `transform-meter` ID that caused a browser error.
- `node --check game.js`, desktop and mobile gameplay checks, and live touch-control check passed without browser errors.

### Active
- Validate transformation activation, transformed skills/visuals, charge attribution, balance, and long-match behavior.
- Review the final changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Retrieve the result of the running `node /tmp/opencode/long-match-check.mjs` check.
2. Run transformation-specific checks, fix any issues, and finish reviewing the changes.
3. Summarize the uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Transformation lifecycle, combat, transformed skills, HUD, input, and visuals.
- `index.html`: Transformation HUD markup.
- `style.css`: Transformation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: Desktop and mobile gameplay assertions.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: Live touch-control check.
- `/tmp/opencode/long-match-check.mjs`: Long-match smoke test.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Browser checks use `http://127.0.0.1:3002`.
- The long-match check is running in the background; transformation-specific validation is pending.

## Objective
- Complete the existing 2D pixel-art 3v3 game with mobile-friendly hero transformations while preserving its roster and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Transformations charge through damage, defeats, and fight participation; can be activated when full; and have limited duration and cooldown.
- Specified heroes need distinct transformed visuals, animations, stronger abilities, improved stats, and start/end visual and sound effects.
- Keep transformations powerful but balanced; heroes without transformations remain playable.
- Transformation bar, button, abilities, and animations must work on mobile.

## Decisions
- Build on the existing dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game.
- Transformation activation uses `T` on keyboard and the visible button on mobile.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added transformation HUD, responsive styling, and transformations for 10 heroes; left other roster heroes playable without transformations.
- Implemented transformation charging/lifecycle, stat and skill changes, effects, sound, visuals, HUD, keyboard/mobile activation.
- Fixed missing `transform-meter` ID that caused a browser error.
- Validated all 10 transformations and 30 transformed skills, charge sources, and mobile activation with no browser errors.
- Desktop/mobile gameplay, victory/defeat, and live touch-control checks passed with no browser errors.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check -- game.js index.html style.css` passed.

- Await the result of the long-match smoke test.
- Finish reviewing the changes.

- (none)

- `game.js`: Transformation lifecycle, combat, transformed skills, HUD, input, and visuals.
- `index.html`: Transformation HUD markup.
- `style.css`: Transformation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/long-match-check.mjs`: Pending long-match smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/transformation-check.mjs`: Transformation-specific browser assertions.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; repository files currently appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Browser checks use `http://127.0.0.1:3002`.

IMPORTANT: Improve Hero Character Designs and Pixel Art

The current hero sprites look poorly designed, blurry, distorted, and difficult to recognize. Completely improve the visual quality of all hero characters.


Requirements:


- Redesign all 13 hero sprites with much better pixel-art quality.
- Make every character clearly recognizable by their hairstyle, clothing, colors, and iconic features.
- Use detailed, clean, carefully arranged pixels instead of blurry or stretched sprites.
- Give every hero unique proportions, animations, and visual effects.
- Add smooth idle, walking, attacking, and ability animations.
- Make characters look like small but detailed 2D anime-inspired pixel-art fighters.
- Keep character proportions consistent across the entire game.
- Improve transformation sprites too, making transformed versions visibly different from normal versions.
- Make sure characters look good on mobile screens and remain easy to recognize during combat.


Use high-quality 2D pixel-art games as visual inspiration. Do not simply enlarge the existing low-quality sprites.


IMPORTANT: Preserve the existing gameplay, hero abilities, progression, and 3v3 system. Focus on improving character artwork and animations.

## Objective
- Improve all 13 hero sprites and animations in the existing 2D pixel-art game while preserving its gameplay, roster, progression, abilities, and 3v3 system.
- Preserve the previously implemented mobile-friendly hero transformations.

## Requirements
- Give all 13 heroes clean, recognizable anime-inspired pixel-art designs with distinct hairstyles, outfits, colors, proportions, and iconic features.
- Add smooth idle, walking, attack, and ability animations; make transformed sprites visibly distinct.
- Ensure characters remain recognizable during combat and on mobile.

## Decisions
- Continue using the existing dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game and draw the sprites directly in `game.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and previously validated transformations, enhanced skills, effects, HUD, keyboard/mobile activation, and responsive styling for the transform-capable heroes.
- Replaced the previous sprite drawing function with detailed roster-specific pixel designs and transformation motifs in `game.js`.
- Adjusted the attack-arm reach animation and roster portrait scale to reduce clipping.

### Active
- Finish wiring pose and transformation state into combat sprite rendering.
- Implement and verify walking, attack, and ability animations and ensure portraits fit their canvases.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Pass transformed state, movement, attack/skill animation timers, and animation time from `drawUnit` to `drawSprite`.
2. Add/update unit animation state and verify that movement and combat trigger the intended poses.
3. Check all roster portraits and transformed visuals for clipping and legibility; run syntax and browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Hero sprite designs, combat rendering, transformations, and game logic.
- `index.html`: Game and HUD markup.
- `style.css`: Canvas and responsive/mobile styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/transformation-check.mjs`: Previously used transformation assertions.
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: Previously used gameplay smoke tests.

- `drawSprite` accepts a `pose` argument, but `drawUnit` still calls it without one; consequently the new transform-specific drawing branch and movement/attack/skill poses are not yet activated in combat.
- `drawSprite` reads `pose.transformed`; the transformed `look` object already carries the hero’s `transform` configuration.
- Project files were untracked in the last reported Git status.

IMPORTANT: Adapt the EXISTING game for mobile phones. Do not create a new game, do not remove existing features, and do not change the 3v3 gameplay.

The current game appears to be designed primarily for desktop keyboards. I want it to be fully playable on Android and iOS touchscreen devices.


Mobile controls


1. Add a virtual joystick on the bottom-left side of the screen for character movement.
2. Add a large basic attack button on the bottom-right side.
3. Add three separate Jutsu ability buttons next to the attack button.
4. Add a transformation button that activates when the transformation bar is full.
5. Make all buttons large enough to use comfortably with fingers.


Mobile interface


- Make the entire game responsive to phone screens.
- Keep health, chakra, and transformation bars visible during combat.
- Make the hero selection screen fit mobile screens.
- Make the "Deploy to Battle" button clearly visible and functional.
- Prevent unwanted page scrolling during gameplay.
- Support both portrait and landscape orientations if possible.


Gameplay


- Make sure the player can actually enter a match.
- Keep the existing 3v3 system with two allied AI heroes and three enemy AI heroes.
- Make the virtual joystick and all action buttons work correctly.
- Keep keyboard controls as an additional option for desktop players.


Testing


Test the complete game on mobile-sized screens.
Verify that the player can select a hero, press Deploy to Battle, enter the arena, move, attack, use Jutsu abilities, and activate transformations.


IMPORTANT: Preserve all existing heroes, abilities, progression, and transformations. Only improve mobile compatibility and fix anything preventing a match from starting.

## Objective
- Improve all 13 heroes’ pixel-art designs and animations while adapting the existing 3v3 game for full mobile touchscreen play.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing game, heroes, abilities, progression, transformations, and 3v3 gameplay; do not create a replacement game or remove features.
- Support Android/iOS touchscreen controls: joystick, basic attack, three separate Jutsu buttons, and transformation activation.
- Make the interface responsive, keep combat vitals visible, fit hero selection and the Deploy button on phones, prevent gameplay scrolling, and support portrait and landscape where possible.
- Keep keyboard controls available on desktop and verify selection, deployment, movement, attacks, abilities, and transformations on mobile-sized screens.

## Decisions
- Continue using the dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game and draw sprites in `game.js`.
- Retain the existing virtual joystick, action buttons, and transformation widget while improving mobile layout and visibility.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented roster-specific pixel-art designs, transformation motifs, and reduced portrait clipping.
- Wired movement, attack, skill, transformation, and animation state into combat sprite rendering.
- Added per-unit movement and attack/skill animation state.
- Verified syntax, transformation behavior, mobile activation, and a live match; inspected desktop and mobile captures.

### Active
- Improving mobile combat layout, touch-target sizing, in-arena health/chakra visibility, and scroll/orientation behavior.
- Added `.mobile-vitals` markup to `index.html`; its styling, JavaScript updates, and mobile testing remain pending.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish responsive combat CSS and update mobile vitals in `game.js`; ensure touch targets are finger-friendly and gameplay does not scroll.
2. Test selection, deployment, joystick movement, attack, all Jutsu buttons, and transformation on mobile-sized portrait and landscape viewports.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, combat HUD updates, touch and keyboard controls, hero sprites, and animations.
- `index.html`: Game, hero selection, mobile controls, transformation widget, and newly added mobile vitals markup.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout, mobile controls, HUD, and touch-target styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: Mobile joystick and skill touch smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/transformation-check.mjs`: Transformation and mobile activation checks.
- `/tmp/opencode/live-match-check.mjs`: Live match smoke test.

## Important Context
- Current project files are uncommitted and appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the current mobile layout work.
- Earlier checks included 10 transformation-enabled heroes and 30 skills, plus a live match ending 1–1 with a defeat result; no browser errors were reported.

- Preserve the existing heroes, abilities, progression, transformations, and 3v3 gameplay.
- Support touchscreen movement, basic attack, three separate Jutsu buttons, and transformation; retain desktop keyboard controls.
- Keep selection and combat responsive, combat vitals visible, prevent scrolling during active mobile matches, and support portrait and landscape where possible.
- Verify hero selection, deployment, movement, attacks, abilities, and transformations on mobile-sized screens.

## Decisions
- Keep the dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game and draw sprites in `game.js`.
- Retain and improve the existing virtual joystick, action buttons, and transformation widget.
- Show compact health and chakra bars in the arena on mobile; hide the side panel and lock scrolling during active matches.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented roster-specific pixel-art designs, transformation motifs, and combat animations.
- Added mobile health/chakra HUD, responsive layouts and touch controls, and active-match scroll locking.
- `node --check game.js` passed; `node /tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs` passed with joystick movement, Jutsu touch, and no browser errors.
- `node /tmp/opencode/transformation-check.mjs` passed for all 10 transformation-enabled heroes and their 30 transformed skills, with no browser errors.

### Active
- Run the new mobile layout/input check across phone portrait, phone landscape, and tablet portrait; inspect selection/deployment fit, touch-control visibility, scrolling, and overlap.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node /tmp/opencode/mobile-layout-check.mjs` and address any layout or interaction failures.
2. Re-run syntax, touch, transformation, and `git diff --check` validations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: combat HUD, touch/keyboard controls, hero sprites, and animations.
- `index.html`: arena, mobile vitals, selection, and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: responsive layout, mobile selection, combat controls, and scroll/orientation behavior.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-layout-check.mjs`: pending multi-viewport mobile layout and input check.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: joystick movement and Jutsu touch test.
- `/tmp/opencode/transformation-check.mjs`: transformation and mobile activation test.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Transformation is supported for 10 heroes; unlock requirements may affect which heroes can be selected in a normal profile.

## Objective
- Improve all 13 heroes’ pixel-art designs and animations while adapting the existing 3v3 game for touchscreen play on phones and tablets.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing heroes, abilities, progression, transformations, and 3v3 gameplay.
- Support touchscreen movement, basic attack, three separate Jutsu buttons, and transformation; retain desktop keyboard controls.
- Keep selection and combat responsive, combat vitals visible, prevent scrolling during active mobile matches, and support portrait and landscape where possible.
- Verify hero selection, deployment, movement, attacks, abilities, and transformations on mobile-sized screens.

- Keep the dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game and draw sprites in `game.js`.
- Retain and improve the existing virtual joystick, action buttons, and transformation widget.
- Show compact health and chakra bars in the arena on mobile; hide the side panel and lock scrolling during active matches.
- Extend responsive styling for 800px-wide tablets and short, touch-enabled landscape screens.

input.prompt: Inspect game.js sprite drawing/render scaling and camera logic. Identify concrete causes of distorted/unclear sprites and propose targeted fixes within existing canvas game. Do not edit; report files/functions and risks. Thoroughness medium.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e5363d024ffeMfLWxB8M7MvUud" state="completed">
## Findings

- **Mobile CSS distorts the entire game canvas.** The canvas is fixed at **480×300** in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html:22` (aspect ratio 1.6), while `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css:2,5–6` gives the frame different ratios on mobile: 1.28, 1.15 on narrow screens, and 1.8 in landscape. The canvas is then forced to `width:100%; height:100%`. During mobile gameplay, `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css:108–117` also sets the frame’s aspect ratio to `auto`, so its dimensions can vary with the available layout space. These mismatches stretch or compress sprites and other game graphics.

- **The sprites are small, and UI marks overlap their heads.** In `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:25–89`, `drawSprite` draws figures roughly 23×39 game pixels, with eyes and several costume details only 1–2 pixels. In `drawUnit` (`game.js:154`), the health bar is drawn *after* the sprite at `y-22`, overlapping its upper hair/head; the player marker at `y-27` also overlaps the hair. That makes already-small character details harder to read.

- **The camera is fixed to the canvas’s logical dimensions.** `game.js:3` defines `W=480, H=300`; `render` (`game.js:144`) centers the camera on the player using those values and clamps it to the world bounds. The camera calculations therefore do not account for the mobile frame’s changed display ratio. At world edges, clamping also means the player is no longer centered, which is expected but worth preserving when adjusting the viewport.

- **The smoothing setting does not address the main scaling issue.** `drawSprite` sets `imageSmoothingEnabled=false` on the context passed to it (`game.js:26`), but these sprites are made from fill rectangles rather than scaled images. The game canvas’s CSS `image-rendering: pixelated` (`style.css:2`) controls scaling of the finished canvas; it cannot correct a mismatched aspect ratio. The `makeSprite` helper (`game.js:24`) appears unused, so changing its smoothing behavior would not fix the live game rendering.

## Targeted fixes

1. **Keep the displayed canvas proportional.** Simplest option: keep the arena at 1.6 on mobile and accept less usable height; alternatively, contain the canvas within the mobile frame and letterbox it. If the game should use the full mobile frame, make the logical render viewport responsive and update camera bounds and ground culling to match. Avoid independently stretching the canvas width and height.

2. **Move the health bar and player marker clear of the head.** In `drawUnit`, place the bar above the sprite’s top (the sprite reaches about `y-31`) and move the player marker above the bar or to a non-overlapping indicator such as the ground ring. This is a localized clarity improvement with little gameplay risk.

3. **Consider a modest, coordinated sprite-size increase.** `drawSprite` already accepts a `scale`; using a slightly larger value for live units could improve readability. Also adjust the related shadow/selection and status UI positions. **Risk:** visuals would become larger than existing collision ranges, and close-packed units could overlap more; this is a visual-only change unless hitboxes are intentionally changed too.

4. **Treat integer-pixel positioning as a polish option, not the primary fix.** `drawSprite` rounds its position and the camera uses floored offsets (`game.js:26,144`), which helps keep the pixel-art body crisp. Other indicators use floating-point positions, so they may not align perfectly with the sprite. Aligning those marks may help, but should follow the aspect-ratio fix.
</subagent>

## Phone gameplay inspection

### Arena and render sizing
- The game canvas is fixed at **480 × 300** in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html:22`. The world is **1320 × 900**, and the camera follows the player while clamping to the world edges (`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:3,144`).
- Desktop arena CSS uses a **1.6:1** aspect ratio, matching the canvas. On mobile, CSS changes the arena to **1.28:1** and then **1.15:1** at narrower widths. During active play, it removes the aspect ratio and lets the frame fill the remaining viewport (`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css:2,5–6,108–117`).
- Because the canvas is styled to fill both the frame’s width and height, these different frame ratios **stretch the 480 × 300 image** rather than showing more of the world. The camera’s visible world area remains fixed.

**Recommendation:** Preserve the canvas’s 1.6:1 ratio in active play, or scale the render viewport/camera for different phone shapes. If the arena must fill the available space, use letterboxing or another deliberate treatment rather than nonuniform stretching.

### Phone controls and overlays
- The touch joystick is anchored at the lower left; four action buttons are grouped at the lower right. The controls occupy a **94px-high bottom strip** in the main mobile rules, reduced to **82px** in landscape and **70px** on shorter landscape screens (`style.css:25–30,83–100`).
- The transformation widget moves to the lower left above the controls: **98px from the bottom** in the main mobile rules, with narrower versions for small phones and landscape (`style.css:10–11,32,42–59,89–100`). Its positioning is designed to sit just above the control strip, but it does cover part of the arena.
- Mobile health and chakra bars replace the side-panel vitals during play. They sit near the top center; the match HUD is near the top edge (`style.css:18–24,108–115`). The side panel is hidden while a phone-sized game is active.
- The viewport is configured for edge-to-edge display, but the inspected CSS does not apply safe-area insets to the shell or HUD. **Check top-edge clearance on notched phones** and consider using `safe-area-inset-*` values.

**Recommendation:** Check the active layout on narrow portrait and short landscape screens, especially the transformation widget’s clearance from the joystick and the amount of visible play area obscured by bottom overlays. Verify top-edge spacing on notched devices.

### Testing and runtime scripts
- No dedicated test/spec files were found in the project inventory.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh` launches the runtime start script; `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh` launches the runtime capture script. Both depend on `RUNTIME_DIR` and invoke scripts under its `scripts/` directory, so they are **runtime utilities, not dedicated test scripts**.
- This was a source inspection; I did not run the game in a phone-sized browser or verify the layout with screenshots.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Improve the existing 3v3 game so Naruto heroes are recognizable and mobile gameplay is comfortable and readable. Preserve existing heroes, abilities, progression, transformations, and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Redesign distorted character art as clear pixel art recognizable as the intended characters.
- Make the arena use phone screen space well, keep the player and nearby enemies visible, and size touch controls comfortably.
- Keep HUD, health/chakra bars, and controls readable without overlap; retain desktop keyboard controls.
- Improve the existing game in place; do not rebuild it.

## Decisions
- Keep the dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game and preserve its existing gameplay.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing code includes roster-specific sprite designs, responsive layouts, touch controls, mobile vitals, and transformation support.

### Active
- Fix canvas/frame aspect-ratio distortion and adapt camera rendering to mobile viewport dimensions.
- Improve sprite scale/readability and prevent health bars and player markers from overlapping characters.
- Verify selection, combat, movement, attacks, abilities, transformations, mobile layout, and browser errors at phone-sized viewports.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `game.js` to size the canvas and camera to the frame, and improve sprite and overhead UI placement.
2. Adjust `style.css` as needed to keep the arena, HUD, and touch controls readable on portrait and landscape screens.
3. Run mobile and gameplay checks, inspect screenshots/layout overlap, and check `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Sprite drawing, combat, inputs, camera, and rendering.
- `style.css`: Arena sizing, responsive layout, HUD, and touch-control positioning.
- `index.html`: Canvas and game/HUD/control markup.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-layout-check.mjs`: Mobile viewport and touch-action checks.
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: Desktop and mobile gameplay checks.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: Real touch input check.
- `/tmp/opencode/transformation-check.mjs`: Transformation and transformed-skill checks.

## Important Context
- `game.js` currently uses fixed `W=480`, `H=300`; mobile CSS changes the frame aspect ratio and stretches the canvas, distorting the game.
- The camera centers on the player but uses those fixed dimensions, so resizing the arena does not adjust the visible world area.
- `drawUnit` draws health bars and the player marker in the character head area; sprite details are small.
- The listed project files were untracked in the latest `git status --short`; no changes were made in the latest inspection.
- A local HTTP server was running at `http://127.0.0.1:3002`.

## Objective
- Improve the existing 3v3 game so Naruto heroes are recognizable and mobile gameplay is comfortable and readable, while preserving the game’s existing content and mechanics.

## Requirements
- Redesign distorted character art as clear pixel art recognizable as the intended characters.
- Use phone screen space well, keep the player and nearby enemies visible, and size touch controls comfortably.
- Keep the HUD, health/chakra bars, and controls readable without overlap; retain desktop keyboard controls.
- Improve the existing game in place; do not rebuild it.

## Decisions
- Keep the dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game and preserve its existing gameplay.

## Work State
### Completed
- `game.js` has roster-specific sprite designs, responsive touch controls and vitals, and transformation support.
- Canvas rendering now adapts to the arena frame without stretching sprites; camera height follows the frame dimensions.
- Overhead health bars and the player marker were repositioned to avoid character overlap.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-layout-check.mjs` passes at portrait, landscape, and tablet viewports, including touch actions and no browser errors.

### Active
- Run the remaining gameplay and transformation checks and inspect browser-visible layouts for remaining overlap or readability issues.

### Blocked

## Objective
- Improve the existing 3v3 game so Naruto characters are recognizable and mobile gameplay is comfortable and readable, while preserving existing content and mechanics.

## Requirements
- Redesign distorted character art as recognizable pixel art.
- Use phone screen space well, keep the player and nearby enemies visible, and size touch controls comfortably.
- Keep the HUD, bars, and controls readable without overlap; retain desktop keyboard controls.
- Improve the existing game in place; do not rebuild it.

## Decisions
- Keep the dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game and preserve its gameplay.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added roster-specific sprites, responsive touch controls and vitals, and transformation support in `game.js`.
- Made canvas rendering responsive without stretching sprites; camera height follows the arena frame.
- Repositioned overhead health bars and the player marker.
- Fixed active mobile layouts so the arena expands to fill available portrait screen space.
- Gameplay, transformation, live-touch, mobile-layout, and browser-error checks passed before the latest CSS-only layout fix; mobile-layout checks passed again after it.

### Active
- Perform final checks and resolve any remaining mobile visual/readability issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Re-run `node /tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`, `node /tmp/opencode/transformation-check.mjs`, and `node /tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`.
2. Recheck the landscape gameplay screenshot and the truncated transformation label.
3. Run `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Sprites, combat, input, camera, canvas sizing, and rendering.
- `style.css`: Arena sizing, HUD, and touch-control positioning.
- `index.html`: Canvas, HUD, and controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: Desktop and mobile gameplay tests.
- `/tmp/opencode/transformation-check.mjs`: Transformation tests.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: Live touch-input test.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-layout-check.mjs`: Mobile viewport and touch-action checks.

## Important Context
- Project files are untracked (`.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, `style.css`); no commit has been made.
- A local HTTP server is available at `http://127.0.0.1:3002`.
- The portrait gameplay screenshot showed the arena filling the screen with controls and squad visible; the landscape screenshot appeared inconsistent with the landscape touch-layout measurements and merits another look.

## Objective
- Improve the existing 3v3 game so Naruto characters are recognizable and mobile gameplay is comfortable and readable, while preserving existing content and mechanics.

## Requirements
- Redesign distorted character art as recognizable pixel art.
- Use phone screen space well, keep the player and nearby enemies visible, and size touch controls comfortably.
- Keep the HUD, bars, and controls readable without overlap; retain desktop keyboard controls.
- Improve the existing game in place; do not rebuild it.

## Decisions
- Keep the dependency-free HTML/CSS/Canvas game and preserve its gameplay.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added roster-specific sprites, responsive touch controls and vitals, and transformation support.
- Made canvas rendering responsive without stretching sprites; camera height follows the arena frame.
- Repositioned overhead health bars and the player marker.
- Made active mobile layouts fill portrait and landscape screens; widened the mobile transformation widget so its full label is visible.
- Gameplay, transformation, live-touch, mobile-layout, browser-error, and `git diff --check` validations passed; portrait and landscape gameplay screenshots were reviewed.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Sprites, combat, input, camera, canvas sizing, and rendering.
- `style.css`: Arena sizing, HUD, touch-control positioning, and mobile layouts.
- `index.html`: Canvas, HUD, and controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/gameplay-check.mjs`: Desktop and mobile gameplay tests.
- `/tmp/opencode/transformation-check.mjs`: Transformation tests.
- `/tmp/opencode/touch-live-check.mjs`: Live touch-input test.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-layout-check.mjs`: Mobile viewport and touch-action checks.

## Important Context
- Project files are untracked (`.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, `style.css`); no commit has been made.
- The transformation label is fully visible at both tested mobile sizes; `documentHeight` matches viewport height during active gameplay.

- Added recognizable, roster-specific pixel-art characters and transformation forms.

- Kept desktop keyboard controls and existing combat mechanics.
